record.paper_title: Observations and Open Questions in Beam-Beam Interactions
record.original_question: Are the observed long-range-loss dependencies on opposing beam intensity and transverse emittance nearly universal for a well-tuned collider operating away from harmful resonances, and if so, do they also hold in the LHC, which has several long-range beam-beam interactions per turn?

evidence.quote: It is possible that these dependencies on (N, ε) are nearly universal for a well tuned machine away from harmful resonances. One machine where this could be tested is the LHC which also has several long-range interactions per turn.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a circular hadron collider in which two counter-rotating bunched beams cross at one or more interaction points and additionally experience several parasitic long-range (electromagnetic) beam-beam encounters per revolution at non-zero transverse separation. For a stored bunch, let the relative particle loss rate L attributable to long-range beam-beam interactions be measured as a function of (i) the opposing beam's bunch intensity N (number of particles per bunch) and (ii) the transverse emittance ε of the opposing beam, while the machine is tuned away from low-order betatron resonances harmful to single-particle stability.

Empirical observations from one such collider show that, in this regime, L exhibits specific functional dependencies on N and ε (e.g., monotone increasing in N and decreasing in ε with characteristic scaling exponents).

Question: Prove or disprove that these observed dependencies of long-range beam-beam loss rate on (N, ε) are essentially universal — i.e., independent of machine-specific parameters — for any well-tuned collider operated away from harmful resonances and possessing several long-range beam-beam encounters per turn. In particular, determine whether the same dependencies govern long-range beam-beam losses in a collider with the geometry and lattice of the Large Hadron Collider (multiple long-range encounters per turn around each of the main interaction points).
artifact.status_search_result: No definitive resolution was located. The question concerns an empirical universality conjecture for long-range beam-beam loss scaling, raised as an open question to be tested at the LHC. Subsequent LHC operational studies have characterized long-range beam-beam effects (e.g., dynamic aperture, diffusion, losses), but a clean confirmation or refutation of strict universality of the (N, ε) dependence across machines does not appear to have been firmly established in the literature reviewed.

status_evidence.title: Observations and Open Questions in Beam-Beam Interactions
status_evidence.snippet: Lists the universality of long-range loss dependence on (N, ε) and its applicability to the LHC as an open question.
status_evidence.claim: The question is explicitly posed as open and proposed to be tested at the LHC.
